entry.title: La Baule Beach
entry.summary: A sweeping semicircular bay of fine pale sand, about 9 km long between Pornichet and Le Pouliguen. It is backed by a seafront promenade and one of the longest beaches in Europe.

entry.title: Cala Galdana
entry.summary: A half-crescent cove of white sand and calm, shallow water on the south coast of Menorca, ringed by pine-covered cliffs. It is a popular family beach with a small resort behind it.

entry.title: Levanto Beach
entry.summary: A wide bay of sand and pebbles in Levanto, a short train ride from the Cinque Terre. It has both free stretches and paid lidos, and a seafront promenade behind.

entry.title: Canyamel Beach
entry.summary: A small sandy beach of roughly 300 m at the mouth of a green valley on the east coast of Mallorca. A freshwater stream sometimes forms a shallow pool behind the sand.

entry.title: Mylopotas Beach
entry.summary: A wide horseshoe bay of golden sand, about 2 km from Chora on Ios. It is the island's busiest beach, with beach bars and tavernas along the shore and hills behind.

entry.title: Cala Agulla
entry.summary: A wide sandy bay on the north-east coast of Mallorca, backed by pine forest and dunes. The sea is clear and shallow, and the bay is roughly 500 to 800 m long.

entry.title: Playa Burriana
entry.summary: The most popular beach in Nerja, about 800 m long and backed by beach bars and restaurants. It has fine dark sand and shallow water, with mountains behind.

entry.title: Kolymbithres Beach
entry.summary: A beach near Naoussa on Paros, known for its smooth, sculpted rock formations that separate small sandy coves. The water is shallow and calm, which suits families.

entry.title: Sa Calobra
entry.summary: A small pebble cove at the end of a winding mountain road in the Serra de Tramuntana. The Torrent de Pareis gorge opens onto the shore nearby, and the water is clear and cool.

entry.title: Cala Sisine
entry.summary: A remote cove in the Gulf of Orosei, where a green canyon opens onto pale sand and shingle. It is reached by boat or on foot, which keeps it quieter than the big resort beaches.

entry.title: Monterosso al Mare
entry.summary: The main beach of the Cinque Terre, at Fegina below the village of Monterosso. It mixes paid lidos with a small free area by the train station, and the sand has pebbles at the water line.

entry.title: Cala Millor
entry.summary: A long, wide sandy bay on the east coast of Mallorca, backed by a palm-lined promenade of restaurants and hotels. Estimates of its length range from about 1.3 km to 2 km.

entry.title: Itzurun Beach
entry.summary: A golden-sand beach of about 270 m in Zumaia, backed by the layered rock cliffs of the Basque flysch coast. The surf can be heavy and low tide reveals the rock formations along the shore.

entry.title: Praia do Baleal
entry.summary: Two sheltered beaches around the small headland of Baleal near Peniche. The north-facing side is about 800 m long and a small island to the west shelters it from the biggest swells, so it suits learners.

entry.title: Paraggi Beach
entry.summary: A small sheltered bay on the Portofino coast, framed by pastel houses and wooded hills. A free public stretch sits in the middle of the beach, with paid lidos at either end.

entry.title: Ses Salines
entry.summary: A long sandy beach at the southern tip of Ibiza, inside the Ses Salines natural park with dunes and pine woods behind. Beach clubs and bars line parts of the sand.

entry.title: Praia de Monte Gordo
entry.summary: A broad, gently sloping beach on the eastern Algarve with shallow water, long sand and a Blue Flag. A promenade runs behind it with restaurants and shops.

entry.title: Kleftiko
entry.summary: A cluster of white rock arches, caves and sheltered coves on the south-west coast of Milos, once used as a pirate hideout. There is no road and no beach facilities, so you swim and snorkel from a boat.

entry.title: Kamari Beach
entry.summary: A long beach of dark volcanic sand and pebbles on the east coast of Santorini, backed by a seafront strip of hotels, cafes and tavernas. Sunbeds and umbrellas line most of the shore.

entry.title: Agiofili Beach
entry.summary: A beach about 2 km from Vasiliki on the south of Lefkada, with clear water and a sandy shore below dry hills. It is reached by road or by boat taxi from the village.

entry.title: Aiguablava Beach
entry.summary: A small sheltered cove near Begur on the Costa Brava, with pine-covered cliffs and clear water. The Parador de Aiguablava stands on the cliff above the beach.

entry.title: Praia de Carcavelos
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach on the Lisbon-Cascais coast, backed by a promenade. Surf schools run lessons here and the beach is reached by train from central Lisbon.

entry.title: Cala Tarida
entry.summary: A west-facing bay on Ibiza with clear water and a curve of sand, popular for evening sunsets. Beach bars and restaurants sit on and above the beach.

entry.title: Playa de Zarautz
entry.summary: The longest beach on the Basque coast, about 2.5 km of golden sand backed by a promenade of bars and restaurants. Several surf schools are based here and the waves suit learners as well as experienced surfers.

entry.title: Cala Rossa
entry.summary: A rocky cove on the island of Favignana in the Egadi Islands, with pale tufa cliffs and clear turquoise water. There is no sand, so people swim from the rocks and flat ledges.

entry.title: Paleokastritsa Beach
entry.summary: A cluster of small coves on the north-west coast of Corfu, backed by green hills and cliffs. Agios Spyridon is the main beach, and boats from the harbour run to sea caves and quieter coves.

entry.title: Plakias Beach
entry.summary: A long sandy beach of about 1.3 km on the south coast of Crete, roughly 40 km from Rethymno. The village behind has tavernas, shops and supermarkets, and quieter stretches lie under the trees.

entry.title: Playa de Calahonda
entry.summary: A small cove in the old town of Nerja, reached through a little arch behind the Balcon de Europa and a zigzag of steps down to the sand. Cliffs frame the beach and the cafes of the town centre are a short walk above.

entry.title: Praia do Barril
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach on the barrier island of the Ria Formosa, reached from Santa Luzia by a flat footpath or a short tourist train. Rows of rusting anchors in the dunes behind the sand are a memorial to the local tuna fishing community.

entry.title: Is Arutas
entry.summary: A beach on the Sinis peninsula in west Sardinia, known for sand made of tiny quartz grains in many colours that give the shallow water a clear, bright look. It is one of the best-known beaches of the Oristano coast.
